items.evidence: horizon-items/src/items.rs LootContext (file byte-identical to 26.1.1's, verified by cmp): (1) condition() (line 1952) reads the kind ONLY from o.get("type") (line 1957) — no dual-form read; 26.1.2's data uses the "condition" key throughout (1,545 occurrences, 0 type-keyed), so every object condition's kind is "" and the match falls to _ => false. conditions() (line 2078) consults the plural "conditions" array, but every element fails. (2) evaluate() applies pool["modifier"]/table["modifier"] (lines 1839-1840), expand() pushes e["modifier"] (line 2112, applied by choose() at line 2221), nested() applies entry["modifier"] (line 2253) — 26.1.2's data has ZERO "modifier" keys and puts functions in "functions" arrays (983: 964 entry/10 pool/9 table), so no function ever runs; modifiers()'s own dual-form discriminator read (f["type"].or(f["function"]), line 2277) is dead code. No normalisation in the load path (loot.rs load_dir lines 773-790 parses files straight into the shared map). Impact over all 1,326 tables: 1,192 carry >=1 condition or >=1 function — blocks 1,052/1,085 (1,023 with a condition), entities 62/108, chests 54/56, gameplay 6/26, dispensers 3/3, equipment 3/3, spawners 3/5, shearing 3/22, harvest 2/3, archaeology 1/6, carve 1/1, charged_creeper 1/6, pots 1/1, brush 0/1; only 134 tables roll correctly. Survival path traced: Game::block_loot_at (game.rs:3683) -> block_drops_by_player (items.rs:1528) -> block_drops_raw (items.rs:1589) -> ctx.evaluate (items.rs:1626/1640) — every conditioned pool/entry is dropped, so survival block-breaking drops nothing from conditioned tables (same symptom the owner confirmed in-game for 1.21.7). /loot routes all table types through this engine too. Post-fix residual recorded here: modifiers() has 12 arms and is missing 7 of the 19 function kinds in the data (copy_components 71 block tables, furnace_smelt 16 entity, set_enchantments 4, set_stew_effect 3, exploration_map 3, set_ominous_bottle_amplifier 3, set_instrument 1 — union 101 tables, verified disjoint fresh from the jar data), and expand() (line 2093) has no minecraft:tag arm (default _ => false, line 2185; the single tag entry, entities/creeper.json); union + tag = 102 tables, exactly the 26.2 run's B12-G01 count. The 26.2 tree reads ["functions"] + dual-form discriminators (items.rs:1969-1970/2246/2387, loot.rs:2040/2053/2153) — the 26.2 playtest fixes were never carried to 26.1.2. Canonical engine item for the merge: Batch 4's B4-G26 (983 functions, 0 modifier, 1,545 condition — all three numbers verified exactly by this batch's census) folds into it.

items.evidence: horizon-world/src/loot.rs is written for the 26.3 loot format throughout (file byte-identical to 26.1.1's, verified by cmp): condition() (line 1368) reads only c["type"] (line 1377); modify() (line 1478) consults singular m["condition"] only (line 1488) while 26.1.2's 184 function-level condition lists are plural "conditions"; run() (line 1512) reads only f["type"] (line 1514) while 26.1.2's 1,404 functions all use the "function" key (default _ => {}, line 1927); table_raw() (line 2011) checks singular pool["condition"] (line 2018) and applies pool/table["modifier"] (lines 2029/2016) while 26.1.2 has 958 plural pool "conditions" arrays and 0 "modifier" keys; expand() (line 2070) checks singular entry["condition"] (line 2071) while 26.1.2's 247 entry lists are plural, so every entry passes its gate; create() (line 2121) applies entry["modifier"] (line 2123); the minecraft:tag arm reads entry["items"] (lines 2100/2136) while 26.1.2's tag entry uses the "name" field. Precision: the file's only f["functions"] read (line 1516) is inside the minecraft:sequence arm of run(), itself unreachable because the discriminator at 1514 reads type only, and minecraft:sequence is not among the 19 function kinds in the data. Every key the engine reads is provably absent from 26.1.2's data (census: 0 modifier keys, 0 type-keyed conditions/functions, 0 singular condition objects), and the engine code is line-for-line the same shape as the 26.1 tree's, which the 26.1 loot_fill run proved broken (7 tables x seeds 1-5: every stack count 1, the gated lava-chicken disc on all 5 zombie seeds, blocks/stone -> minecraft:stone, blocks/diamond_ore -> minecraft:diamond_ore). loot_fill was NOT re-run for 26.1.2: the brief's byte-identical-code condition is met (both loot files cmp-identical to 26.1.1's), so the live demonstration for 26.1.2 specifically remains unproven. Batch 0's oracle table separately records VanillaLootFillOracle failing to compile on all three classpaths (missing-symbol, 1 error) — an oracle matter for the owning batch, not this one. Affects entity drops, chest/container loot, fishing, trial spawners and vaults. 0 additional gap checks: these tables are already counted under items.rs (B12-G01).

items.evidence: crafting.rs Ingredient::parse_object (line 123) requires a neoforge:ingredient_type or type key and returns None otherwise, so vanilla object forms ({"item": "..."}, {"tag": "..."}) fail to parse and the recipe is dropped. No vanilla 26.1.2 recipe uses object ingredients (5,168 string slots + 115 array slots whose 1,151 elements are all strings, counted as occurrences; 0 object slots — the firework star's shapes map is shape name -> string ingredient), so this affects only player datapack / mod recipes using the object form. Same code and same data property as 1.21.7's B12-G05 and 26.2's B12-G02.
items.title: Object-form recipe ingredients are rejected (datapack scope only)

items.evidence: crafting.rs:1739: time: v["cookingtime"].as_u64().unwrap_or(200) — a flat 200-tick default for all four cooking types. Vanilla 26.1.2's per-type defaults, verified by javap -c on the client jar (the int each recipe class passes to AbstractCookingRecipe.cookingMapCodec): smelting 200, blasting 100, smoking 100, campfire_cooking 100. A datapack blasting/smoking/campfire recipe without cookingtime would cook at 200 ticks instead of 100. All 116 vanilla cooking recipes carry explicit cookingtime (smelting 73, blasting 25, smoking 9, campfire 9), so no vanilla recipe is affected. The 26.2 tree uses per-type defaults (crafting.rs:1745-1759).

systemic_note: The prepared data is faithful — all 5,309 data-driven files byte-identical to the 26.1.2 jar, block-tags.json byte-faithful too. The 1.21.7 systemic finding (code reading the 26.x form of formats the version writes differently) DOES carry to 26.1.2: 26.1.2 writes the OLD loot forms (condition/function discriminators, plural conditions arrays, functions arrays, tag-entry name) while both engines in the 26.1.2 tree read the 26.3 forms (type, modifier, singular condition, tag items), and the 26.2 playtest fixes that taught the engines both forms were never carried to the 26.1.2 tree. Everything else in scope is clean: specials are data-driven, the effect table legitimately has 40 entries, and the recipe/advancement/tag/enchantment/damage loaders all read 26.1.2's forms correctly.
